#philosophy #teaching

*Republic* Book VII, 514a to 520a, Grube's translation revised by Reeve (Hackett, 1992), p. 186. Prisoners chained since childhood, facing a wall, a fire behind them, people carrying figures along a low parapet so the shadows pass in front. The shadows are all they know. One is freed, dragged up the steep ascent, dazzled by the sun, and only slowly able to look at things themselves. When he goes back down, half blind in the dark, the others laugh and would kill him if they could, which is Socrates' own fate in 399 BC. Did it with TY on 22 January 2025: blinds down, a desk lamp behind a bedsheet, cardboard cut-outs of a dog, a bus and the principal. Ellen asked if Instagram is the cave. Liam asked who the puppeteers are now, and we lost the rest of the class to that, happily. Next year: pair it with [[Gettier cases]] on what counts as knowing, and with [[Ethics of AI]] on screens.
